title: Adverse Event Intake from Emails and Calls
summary: Spot possible adverse events in emails, call recordings and field reports, extract the minimum case criteria and draft an intake record for your pharmacovigilance team to verify.

seo.title: AI Adverse Event Intake for Pharmacovigilance | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that finds possible adverse events in emails, calls and field reports, extracts case details and drafts intake records for PV team review.

problem.intro: Possible adverse events reach a pharma company through many doors: the medical information inbox, customer care calls, product complaints, MR visit notes and distributor emails. Each one has to be recognised, captured with enough detail to form a valid case and passed to the safety database within reporting timelines.

pain_points.title: Events hidden in other conversations
pain_points.detail: A packaging complaint or a stock query may mention that a patient felt dizzy, and front-line staff do not always recognise it as safety information.

pain_points.title: Incomplete first reports
pain_points.detail: Intake forms often miss reporter contact details, the suspect product batch or the event onset date, which triggers repeated follow-ups.

pain_points.title: The clock starts at first receipt
pain_points.detail: Reporting timelines run from when any employee first receives the information, so a report sitting in a field rep's notes is already ageing.

pain_points.title: Manual re-keying
pain_points.detail: Safety associates retype narratives and fields from emails into the safety database, which is slow and invites transcription errors.

solution.overview: We build an intake layer that watches the channels you choose, such as the medical information mailbox, customer care call recordings and MR call reports, and flags text that may describe an adverse event, special situation or product complaint. For each flagged item it extracts the four minimum criteria for a valid case, plus product, batch, dose, dates and outcome where present, and drafts an intake form and narrative with each field linked to its source sentence. Calls in Hindi and other Indian languages are transcribed first. Your PV team verifies, completes and submits; the system never assesses seriousness or causality.
capabilities: Screens emails, call transcripts, MR reports and complaint records for possible adverse events and special situations
Extracts identifiable patient, reporter, suspect product and event: the minimum criteria for a valid case
Captures batch, dose, onset date, outcome and concomitant medicines when mentioned
Transcribes and translates calls in Hindi and regional languages, keeping the original text
Drafts an intake form and narrative with every field linked to its source
Records the first-receipt date and time for each report to support timeline tracking

workflow.title: Monitor intake channels
workflow.detail: Connectors pull new emails, call recordings, MR reports and complaint records from the agreed channels.

workflow.title: Transcribe and screen
workflow.detail: Calls are transcribed, and every item is screened for possible adverse events, special situations and complaints.

workflow.title: Extract case details
workflow.detail: For flagged items, the minimum criteria and other case details are extracted with links to the source text.

workflow.title: Draft the intake
workflow.detail: An intake form and narrative are drafted, with missing criteria listed as follow-up questions instead of being filled in.

workflow.title: Safety associate verifies
workflow.detail: A drug safety associate reviews the draft, corrects fields, decides whether it is a valid case and requests follow-up if needed.

workflow.title: Hand over to the safety database
workflow.detail: The verified intake goes into the safety database through an import or form, with the audit trail attached.

inputs: Medical information and customer care emails
MR call reports and field notes
Product master with brand and generic names
outputs: Screening result per item: possible adverse event, special situation, complaint or none
Draft intake form with minimum criteria and case details
Draft narrative linked to source sentences
Follow-up question list for missing information
human_in_the_loop: A trained drug safety associate verifies every flagged item and decides whether it is a valid case. Seriousness, expectedness, causality and MedDRA coding are confirmed by your PV team, and PV samples items screened as no event to check for misses.
integrations: Safety database such as Oracle Argus, ArisGlobal LifeSphere or an in-house system
Email platform such as Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace
Pharma CRM used by the field force
guardrails: Screening tuned to favour catching events, with PV sampling of items screened as no event
No field is filled unless the source text supports it
Original-language text kept alongside every translation
Patient and reporter details masked in logs and restricted by role
Models and prompts under change control
compliance_notes: Supports the pharmacovigilance obligations of marketing authorisation holders, including adverse drug reaction reporting in India under CDSCO and PvPI guidance.
Output fields can be structured towards ICH E2B(R3) data elements for downstream case submission.
Patient and reporter data is handled in line with the DPDP Act 2023 and, where relevant, GDPR.

pilot.scope: One intake channel, such as the medical information mailbox, using historical emails already triaged by your PV team, followed by a short live parallel run.
deliverables: Screening and extraction configured for your product portfolio
Review queue for drug safety associates
Comparison report against your historical triage decisions
List of missed and false flags with root causes

what_we_measure.how: Historical items your PV team classed as adverse events, checked for whether the system flagged them.
Flagged items the safety associate marks as not an adverse event.
Draft intake fields compared with the values in the final verified case.
Timestamps from first receipt to verified intake, with and without the system.

faqs.q: What if the system misses an adverse event?
faqs.a: Screening is set to favour catching possible events over avoiding false flags, and PV reviews a sample of items marked as no event. The pilot measures misses against your own historical triage, so you can see the risk before going live.

faqs.q: Can it handle calls in Hindi or other Indian languages?
faqs.a: Yes. Calls are transcribed in the original language and translated, and the reviewer sees both versions. The pilot reports accuracy for each language you include.

faqs.q: Does it submit reports to regulators?
faqs.a: No. It prepares intake drafts. Case assessment, coding and regulatory submission remain with your PV team and safety database.
Data stays in your cloud tenancy or on-premise, access is role-based, and personal identifiers are masked in logs. We use model endpoints that do not retain or train on your data.
